approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two highest-scoring earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current elites, preserving their original accepted strings and scores. The policy fits all selected sequences with equal weight toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward. It takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps and uses the final policy to sample complete SMILES; chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refill the next batch. A passive uniform-history comparator measures the retained score-ordered replay mechanism without contributing to training.
approach.novelty: Add best-prefix checkpoint restoration to online adaptation: after following the existing bounded Adam update path, keep the visited policy and matching optimizer state with the lowest training loss, including the unchanged starting state as an option. This addresses the observed cases where the final iterate has already made the selected examples fit worse. The change selects which completed update prefix survives; it uses the same targets, examples, equal weights and gradient calculations. Earlier siblings changed prior learning, replay membership or retention, and equivalent training strings. None tested whether the last online iterate should be replaced by a better state already visited during the same update. A comparison with the discarded final iterate will establish activation separately from later molecular novelty and score.

hypothesis: Retain the policy and matching Adam optimizer checkpoint with the lowest unchanged combined current-and-historical augmented-target mean squared error among the starting state and every iterate visited by the inherited bounded online update, choosing the earliest exact tie instead of automatically retaining the last iterate.

finding_summary.headline: Earlier checkpoints lowered training loss but reduced final scores in all three seeds
finding_summary.insights:
Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.
finding_summary.results:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Of 435 updates followed by new proposals, 142 retained an earlier policy and matching Adam state: five initialization updates and 137 later feedback updates. Every intervention produced a measurable parameter difference from its discarded endpoint. On those same update paths, terminal-minus-selected mean squared error averaged 0.202718, summing to 28.785889. All 450 updates, including 15 terminal updates, retained the minimum logged loss on the fixed training tensor. Seven early sitagliptin updates retained their starting state. Targets, training membership, equal row weights and the executed Adam rule remained unchanged.

Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.513272 to 0.487621, a paired mean change of -0.025651; the individual seed changes were -0.036109, -0.010057 and -0.030788. Population standard deviation increased from 0.001984 to 0.012470. Four of five task means fell, led by sitagliptin from 0.288538 to 0.197063; drd2 was essentially unchanged. Both algorithms delivered all 4,350 novel accepted optimizer proposals. Canonical-novel yield among raw draws rose from 51.81% to 52.79%, and distinct chemical-core coverage increased on four tasks. Those coverage improvements did not provide the predicted score gain.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and cyclic chemistry, but recurring high-score cores, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth.
molecular.overall_character: The read trajectories cover every listed objective. These molecules are predominantly recognizable medicinal-chemistry scaffolds: aryl and heteroaryl amides, fused heteroarenes, sulfonamides, ethers, hydrazones and saturated nitrogen heterocycles. The optimizer proposal ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9747 to 0.9989 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9391 to 0.9954; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 37.8 to 51.1 characters and are not molecular-weight measurements. Structural diversity is moderate across the complete trajectories and seeds, with much narrower families among many high-scoring samples. Ring formation, aromatic nitrogen and basic cyclic amines are demonstrated capabilities. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, including outputs with complex saturated ring junctions, so molecular chirality is often left unspecified. The explicit charged_rate does not measure whether neutral amines can protonate. Conventional scaffolds look synthetically plausible, but highly elaborate ring assemblies, unusual heteroatom linkages and extreme hydrocarbon growth make the overall synthetic reading questionable. Stability, ionization, solubility and synthetic-route concerns below are structural interpretations, not measured properties. Parent comparisons describe observed chemistry and recorded scores only; they do not establish mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The highest digest samples are compact, predominantly planar aza-carbazole-type fused heteroarenes whose ring nitrogen bears a methylene carboxamide joined to a methoxyphenyl or methoxypyridyl group. They contain an amide donor/carbonyl acceptor, an ether and variably placed pyridine-like nitrogens. Other trajectories include azaindole ester/carboxamides and arylamine, sulfonamide and hydroxy-fused-arene families. The worst samples are much larger assemblies with extended hydrocarbon ester tails, bulky saturated nitrogen rings or elaborate oxygenated ring systems. Amide formation and substitution of an available heterocyclic building block are plausible synthetic disconnections for the leading series; the fused aza-core still requires an appropriate precursor. Relative to the Parent, the leading chemistry in seed 1 changes from substituted pyrazole carboxamides to aza-carbazole acetamides, while seed 0 retains the same leading azaindole ester/amide family. This is a change in scaffold arrangement within already abundant ring chemistry.
liabilities: The leading aza-carbazole family has a substantial planar aromatic surface, leaving aqueous behavior and solid-state packing uncertain.
Very long alkyl ester appendages and oversized multifunctional assemblies are still proposed despite their extremely small recorded scores.
Late proposals include hydrazides, a free aryl thiol and adjacent phenols; these add unassessed chemical behavior beyond the leading amide series.
missing_features: The poor proposals often lose the compact combination of aromatic heteroatom placement, an amide linker and limited peripheral bulk seen in the stronger examples; merely retaining aromatic rings does not preserve that arrangement.

The highest digest samples give little coverage of alternative ring topologies carrying a comparable donor/acceptor arrangement, although the Parent supplies a distinct high-scoring pyrazole-amide family.
A specific absent target motif cannot be identified from this score span; the supported gap is reliable coverage of balanced compact arrangements rather than absence of ring or nitrogen chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxypyridyl aza-carbazole acetamide and the methoxyphenyl diaza analogue both score 0.46671988179915697. A closely related methoxyphenyl aza analogue scores 0.46331566856387824, while other aromatic-nitrogen placements score 0.4418627361103939. The visible neighborhood supports particular heteroatom positions within a compact aromatic-amide arrangement, without a simple benefit from adding more nitrogens. The initial methoxyindole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the large ring/amine assembly scores 9.068393833650252e-27 and the long-chain indole ester scores 3.13726955652741e-24. Final proposals still range from a larger aminopolyaryl amide at 0.0009912168585955116 to a more compact diarylamine carboxamide at 0.41220436185971376. The Parent seed-1 leading pyrazole carboxamide scores 0.4697065314067379, so the Child examples do not show that this fused core is uniquely required.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large polyaromatics with dense fluorine substitution. A prominent family is an aryl acylhydrazone connected to a diarylamine; another combines pyridyl and phenyl rings with a thiazolylmethoxy linkage. A further family uses an aryl thiourea connected through an aminomethylene/imine chain to another arene or azaarene. Final samples add bromine, nitro groups and additional aromatic nitrogens. The optimizer halogen_rate is 0.8724, consistent with this strong substitution bias. Hydrazone condensation, thiourea formation and ether connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry, although dense positional substitution and undefined imine geometry complicate the identity of a physical product. Parent trajectories already contain polyfluoroaryl hydrazones and thiourea/imines; the Parent seed-1 leading thioalkyl-pyridyl aminoalkyl family is replaced among the Child leaders by thiazolylmethoxy-pyridyl chemistry.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces and extensive fluorine or heavier-halogen substitution increase hydrophobic structural burden; aqueous properties were not measured here.
Hydrazones and imines introduce possible hydrolysis, geometric-isomer and tautomer concerns, while thioureas add further tautomeric and chemical variability.
Nitro substitution persists in the final thiourea/imine molecules, so substantial chemical liabilities can coexist with scores near those of the leading examples.
missing_features: The high-scoring examples provide limited coverage of less halogen-loaded, more conformationally varied versions of their recurring aromatic donor/acceptor arrangements. Their scores do not establish whether those alternatives would be favored.
The leading acylhydrazone and thiourea/imine series do not specify the configuration of their imine bonds; a defined geometric chemical identity is missing from those strings.
The available gradients identify local aromatic substitution patterns, but cannot establish a unique missing target-specific scaffold or a universal linker requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated acylhydrazone scores 0.6010573047491092. Closely related benzoyl substitution patterns score 0.5989441930618401 and 0.597835391953039, making local fluorine placement/addition a visible source of small changes within this family. The distinct thiazolylmethoxy compound scores 0.5999139813405677 and the aryl thiourea/imine scores 0.5966118931649093. Thus several linkers can support similar recorded values. The fluorophenyl sulfonyl cyanide scores 0.25700280112044815, a larger polyaryl sulfone 0.26617434238528986 and a cyclic-sulfone thiourea 0.286193233770192; trifluoromethane scores 0.5004402958788305. These observations do not support a monotonic molecular-size or general-quality interpretation. The Parent seed-1 aminoalkyl pyridine reaches 0.6039526921879863 with a different linker arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of alkyl-substituted indoles attached to piperidine rings whose free tertiary nitrogen carries a haloarylalkyl group. These are medium-to-large molecules combining aromatic hydrophobic surfaces, an indole NH and a potentially protonatable aliphatic nitrogen. Another strong family contains phenolic spirocyclic amine polycycles with chloroaryl ether-containing appendages; final samples also carry primary amines, alcohol/phenol groups and related saturated-ring changes. The leading indole/piperidine connectivity looks compatible with conventional heterocycle assembly and N-alkylation, while the spiro/fused products pose greater ring-construction and stereochemical demands. Low examples are aromatic amides, oxalamides, hydrazones and sulfonamides, often with their nitrogen functionality conjugated to carbonyl or sulfonyl groups. The Parent also generated strong aryl cyclic amines, but its leading families included piperazine/pyrrolidine arrangements and flexible alkyl diamines. The Child visibly explores more indole-centered and spiro/bridged cyclic amine chemistry.
liabilities: Alkyl tails, multiple aromatic surfaces and halogens give many leading compounds considerable hydrophobic burden alongside their basic nitrogen.
Complex spiro/fused ring assemblies are incompletely specified without stereochemistry, and their scores do not demonstrate an accessible synthesis of a defined isomer.
Formal neutral SMILES do not resolve protonation state for these amines; actual ionization and assay behavior remain unmeasured.
missing_features: The weak sulfonamide/amide examples lack the free aliphatic nitrogen environment and spatial aromatic/basic-group combination repeatedly present among the stronger molecules. The generator already demonstrates that capability in its leading families.
The saturated spiro and fused structures lack specified relative or absolute stereochemistry despite ring junctions and substituents that can create distinct stereoisomers.

There is limited high-score evidence for preserving the observed aromatic/basic arrangement while reducing bulky alkyl and halogen appendages; the trajectories do not establish which smaller alternatives would retain the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propylindole/tertiary-piperidine haloarylalkyl molecules score 0.9999999595806517, and a phenolic spirocyclic amine scores 0.9999996167758578. The low anisamide/heteroaryl sulfonamide scores 1.9828327575562915e-05; its piperidine nitrogen is sulfonyl-bound, so the ring does not supply the same free aliphatic amine environment as the leading piperidines. A neutral aryl oxalamide scores 3.0069171067466083e-05. This supports the joint arrangement of an available aliphatic basic center and aromatic surface in these trajectories. It does not establish that a basic nitrogen alone suffices: the initial molecule with a free N-methylpiperidine, amide and hydroxamic-acid group scores 0.0003786988088202195. These are recorded objective values, not binding affinities, and the molecules alone do not identify a unique receptor interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large heteroatom-rich ring assemblies: fused aromatic carbonyl heterocycles bearing sulfonamide-linked morpholine or diazacycles, as well as benzodioxole-containing aryl heterocycles. The leading molecule combines an aryl-fused oxygen heterocycle, a ketone/exocyclic imine and a morpholine sulfonamide. Related samples include lactams, piperazines, aryl ureas and fused azaarenes. Their amide and sulfonamide connections are synthetically recognizable, though the imino-carbonyl and densely substituted fused cores need closer chemical definition. The worst samples include a small chlorinated N-hydroxyformamide, flexible peptide-like chains, long alkyl chains and small imino heterocycles. Parent leaders more often combine aryl/fused carbonyl cores with substituted piperazine sulfonamides, while the Child seed-0 leader retains a morpholine sulfonamide and other Child seeds sample broader aryl heterocycles. Both generations contain the constituent ring and polar-group chemistry.
liabilities: Leading and near-leading structures include imino-carbonyl and quinone-like dicarbonyl systems with additional stability, tautomeric or redox questions.
A sulfonyl-bound morpholine or diazacycle nitrogen is chemically different from a free basic amine; a count of nitrogen rings would conceal that distinction.
Some late molecules accumulate fused and pendant aromatic rings without preserving the stronger examples' full polar arrangement.
missing_features: The lowest samples omit the combined aromatic framework, carbonyl/sulfonyl acceptor pattern and cyclic polar substituent found in stronger structures; adding a small heterocycle or a flexible amide chain does not recreate that arrangement.

Late proposals do not consistently retain the combined polar fused-core and substituted diazacycle/sulfonamide arrangements seen among Parent and early Child leaders. These substructures are available, but their useful joint configurations are not consistently represented.
The exocyclic imine of the leading structure lacks a defined geometric state, and the provided examples do not establish a more specific missing target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The morpholine-sulfonamide imino ketone scores 0.20325754327905224 at evaluation 91, followed by a fused diazacycle sulfonamide/lactam at 0.20120147126513588 and a piperazine/heteroaryl sulfonamide at 0.19718878121013778. In contrast, the ring-free chlorinated N-hydroxyformamide scores 0.007693218186208301, the peptide-like molecule 0.025041397240195853 and a small imino sulfur heterocycle 0.0345361852497211. Several rings plus a spatially organized aromatic/polar combination distinguish these higher examples; many amide groups alone do not. A late polyaryl piperazinyl carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.18230155742745996, whereas the simpler benzyl tetrahydroisoquinoline scores 0.11757927025044308. The Parent fused carbonyl/arylpiperazine sulfonamide reaches 0.2354681799202668. These comparisons support arrangement-sensitive chemistry rather than an unobserved universal functional-group requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The isolated stronger molecules are compact-to-medium nitrogen-rich heteroarenes and carbonyl-linked aryl compounds. The leader is a methylamino/methyl-substituted triazine carboxamide attached to a dimethylphenyl group. Other examples include an amino/hydroxy fused heterocycle with a saturated tertiary nitrogen, a fused azaarene N-oxide carboxamide, aryl/furanylmethyl oxalamides and an aryl/pyridyl oxalamide. These have recognizable amide or oxalamide synthesis opportunities and limited peripheral bulk compared with the worst outputs. The broader trajectory also emits very long hydrocarbon chains, elaborate steroid-like esters, peptide-like assemblies and large nitrogen-containing rings. Parent leaders include pyrazole carboxamide alcohols, fused azaheteroaryl benzamides and aryl acylhydrazones; the Child shifts toward aminotriazine carboxamides and oxalamides. Compact heteroatom-rich chemistry is present in both generations, but widely different and oversized structures persist through final evaluations.
liabilities: Extreme hydrocarbon growth produces very large flexible or macrocyclic structures, including a zero-scoring nitrogen ring with extensive alkyl content.
Other poor samples accumulate peptide-like donor/acceptor arrays or elaborate polycyclic ester frameworks, so excess polarity and complexity are also represented.

Furan, N-oxide, adjacent oxalamide carbonyls and tautomeric amino/hydroxy heteroarenes introduce distinct chemical behavior among the stronger molecules; none has demonstrated stability, solubility or a completed synthesis here.
missing_features: Much of the output lacks the simultaneous limited hydrocarbon burden, positioned nitrogen heteroatoms and compact carbonyl-linked donor/acceptor arrangement found among the isolated stronger examples.

The final molecules do not consistently preserve or closely explore the aminotriazine and oxalamide arrangements already associated with higher observed scores; chemically distinct oversized families continue to appear.
Specified stereochemistry is absent even in complex saturated-ring outputs, although the shown scores do not establish that a particular stereochemical motif is required.
The sparse, structurally heterogeneous higher examples leave any unique missing target-specific group indeterminate.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminotriazine carboxamide scores 0.26223613784124133 against a digest median of 1e-06. The fused amino/hydroxy heterocycle scores 0.20803336453696816 and the azaarene N-oxide carboxamide 0.198169175615563. The dimethylphenyl/furanylmethyl oxalamide scores 0.19770893824865138, while its less methyl-substituted aryl counterpart scores 0.13923463506082193; this local comparison supports tuned composition within a compact polar framework, not simply making every molecule smaller. The pyridyl oxalamide scores 0.18652622280944445. The enormous hydrocarbon-rich nitrogen ring and elaborate steroid-like ester each score 0.0, and a final long-chain aryl heterocyclic ketone scores 4.064637608571372e-56. Compactness and heteroatoms are insufficient by themselves: a final small aryl/azaaryl acetamide scores 0.002351936446697417. The Parent fused azaheteroaryl benzamide reaches 0.30950439639437716 with a different topology. The heterogeneous maxima do not identify one missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Strong phenolic spirocyclic amines and later fused-ring products contain saturated junctions and substituted ring atoms without tetrahedral stereochemical notation. Leading hydrazone and imine strings also leave their double-bond geometry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not supply defined stereochemical alternatives for its complex saturated-ring products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve chemically coherent stereochemical states as part of proposed molecular identity, including relevant ring-junction and imine alternatives. Available feedback can then distinguish defined structures; these trajectories provide no evidence favoring a particular isomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high-score excerpts repeatedly show aza-carbazole acetamides, haloarylalkyl indole-piperidines or polyfluoroaryl hydrazones. Full trajectories and Parent examples contain alternative useful pyrazole amides, substituted diazacycle sulfonamides and other cyclic amines. Broad global chemical variety coexists with narrow local high-score families.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring molecular support often contracts to substituent variants of a small number of ring and linker families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain score-supported alternatives in core topology and linker connectivity as chemically distinct generative support, so new accepted identities can explore more than aromatic nitrogen positions, halogen substitutions and peripheral alkyl changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest examples include a long-chain aromatic ester scoring 3.13726955652741e-24, a hydrocarbon-rich nitrogen macrocycle scoring 0.0 and a final long-chain heteroaryl ketone scoring 4.064637608571372e-56. Compact heteroaryl amides and oxalamides occur among stronger examples, while substantial alkyl and ring burden can still accompany high-scoring basic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control hydrocarbon and scaffold growth while retaining compact polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled changes in substituent size, linker length and polar-group placement around multiple retained cores. Use the observed score context to maintain a suitable size/polarity balance within each chemical family, without imposing one molecular-size preference on all feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring acylhydrazones and thiourea/imine chains recur, an imino-carbonyl ring leads another excerpt, and late samples add nitro groups, hydrazides or a free aryl thiol. Conventional amide and ether connections are also demonstrated elsewhere in the generated set, so these alternatives are chemically within the generator's reach.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some strong aromatic arrangements are explored mainly through geometrically or chemically ambiguous linkers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden chemically coherent linker and tautomer alternatives around score-supported aromatic arrangements, preserving their actual donor/acceptor environments and geometric identity. Treat the recorded objective value and the chemical definition or plausible stability of a product as separate observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Strong indole-piperidine and spirocyclic examples contain free aliphatic amines, whereas weak piperidine sulfonamides place nitrogen next to sulfonyl groups. Elsewhere compact aromatic amides outperform peptide-like chains despite abundant nitrogen and carbonyl groups in both. The structures show that heteroatom presence alone does not capture the useful chemical configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve ionization-relevant nitrogen environments together with their supporting ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and explore the full local ring/linker/functional-group environment, distinguishing free amines, amides, sulfonamides and aromatic nitrogens as chemical states. Let the available score feedback determine which complete arrangements remain useful.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

activation_observables.measurement: For every actual training member, independently join the unchanged accepted record and original sequence, recompute frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times its accepted score, and verify equal row weights and fixed current/history membership across every candidate prefix. Record positive targets and target-minus-starting-likelihood signs without correcting them. Confirm that the passive uniform members remain diagnostic-only and that no diagnostic-only current nonelite enters the checkpoint-selection loss.
activation_observables.name: Recompute every selected member's target from its unchanged accepted score and frozen-prior likelihood; record target attainability, target-minus-starting-likelihood sign and the specific target/weight/update change on fixed inputs.

activation_observables.measurement: Preserve the inherited fixed-pre-update current-only, historical-only and actual combined gradient receipts and verify the same unclipped mean-loss gradient calculation precedes the unchanged clipped Adam path. Log all visited prefix losses, executed step count and selected prefix. Define an intervention opportunity as terminal combined eval-mode loss exceeding the minimum visited loss by tolerance 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(abs(terminal_loss), abs(minimum_loss)). On every such opportunity, the retained prefix must precede the terminal prefix and its policy and complete optimizer state must match the recorded selected snapshot exactly. Measure retained-versus-terminal policy distance with tolerance 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(retained_update_norm, terminal_update_norm); register a measurable difference on at least one nonterminal intervention opportunity. Report initialization, later feedback and terminal updates separately. The discarded endpoint is a same-path comparator on the Child's actual batch, not a counterfactual scored Parent trajectory.
activation_observables.name: Measure current-only, historical-only and actual combined gradients at identical pre-update parameters; for a weighting or update mechanism, verify changed gradient contributions and realized parameter updates without diagnostic optimizer steps.

activation_observables.measurement: Recompute selected, starting and terminal losses on the identical selected sequences in eval mode with the same fixed targets. The emitted policy loss must equal the minimum visited prefix loss within 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(abs(selected_loss),abs(minimum_loss)), and must not exceed starting or terminal loss beyond the corresponding tolerance. Register positive pooled terminal-minus-selected loss over nonterminal intervention opportunities. Report no-op and no-opportunity counts, current/history group and per-row before/after residuals and both likelihood directions. finding_summary.headline: Earlier checkpoints lowered training loss but reduced final scores in all three seeds
finding_summary.insights:
Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.
finding_summary.results:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Of 435 updates followed by new proposals, 142 retained an earlier policy and matching Adam state: five initialization updates and 137 later feedback updates. Every intervention produced a measurable parameter difference from its discarded endpoint. On those same update paths, terminal-minus-selected mean squared error averaged 0.202718, summing to 28.785889. All 450 updates, including 15 terminal updates, retained the minimum logged loss on the fixed training tensor. Seven early sitagliptin updates retained their starting state. Targets, training membership, equal row weights and the executed Adam rule remained unchanged.

Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. Both algorithms delivered all 4,350 novel accepted optimizer proposals. Canonical-novel yield among raw draws rose from 51.81% to 52.79%, and distinct chemical-core coverage increased on four tasks. finding_summary.insights:
Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.
finding_summary.results:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. finding_summary.headline: Earlier checkpoints lowered training loss but reduced final scores in all three seeds
finding_summary.insights:
Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.
finding_summary.results:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Of 435 updates followed by new proposals, 142 retained an earlier policy and matching Adam state: five initialization updates and 137 later feedback updates. Every intervention produced a measurable parameter difference from its discarded endpoint. On those same update paths, terminal-minus-selected mean squared error averaged 0.202718, summing to 28.785889. All 450 updates, including 15 terminal updates, retained the minimum logged loss on the fixed training tensor. Seven early sitagliptin updates retained their starting state. Targets, training membership, equal row weights and the executed Adam rule remained unchanged.

Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.513272 to 0.487621, a paired mean change of -0.025651; the individual seed changes were -0.036109, -0.010057 and -0.030788. Population standard deviation increased from 0.001984 to 0.012470. Four of five task means fell, led by sitagliptin from 0.288538 to 0.197063; drd2 was essentially unchanged. Both algorithms delivered all 4,350 novel accepted optimizer proposals. Canonical-novel yield among raw draws rose from 51.81% to 52.79%, and distinct chemical-core coverage increased on four tasks. Those coverage improvements did not provide the predicted score gain.

molecular_assessment.headline: Rich aromatic and cyclic chemistry, but recurring high-score cores, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The read trajectories cover every listed objective. These molecules are predominantly recognizable medicinal-chemistry scaffolds: aryl and heteroaryl amides, fused heteroarenes, sulfonamides, ethers, hydrazones and saturated nitrogen heterocycles. The optimizer proposal ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9747 to 0.9989 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9391 to 0.9954; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 37.8 to 51.1 characters and are not molecular-weight measurements. Structural diversity is moderate across the complete trajectories and seeds, with much narrower families among many high-scoring samples. Ring formation, aromatic nitrogen and basic cyclic amines are demonstrated capabilities. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, including outputs with complex saturated ring junctions, so molecular chirality is often left unspecified. The explicit charged_rate does not measure whether neutral amines can protonate. Conventional scaffolds look synthetically plausible, but highly elaborate ring assemblies, unusual heteroatom linkages and extreme hydrocarbon growth make the overall synthetic reading questionable. Stability, ionization, solubility and synthetic-route concerns below are structural interpretations, not measured properties. Parent comparisons describe observed chemistry and recorded scores only; they do not establish mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The highest digest samples are compact, predominantly planar aza-carbazole-type fused heteroarenes whose ring nitrogen bears a methylene carboxamide joined to a methoxyphenyl or methoxypyridyl group. They contain an amide donor/carbonyl acceptor, an ether and variably placed pyridine-like nitrogens. Other trajectories include azaindole ester/carboxamides and arylamine, sulfonamide and hydroxy-fused-arene families. The worst samples are much larger assemblies with extended hydrocarbon ester tails, bulky saturated nitrogen rings or elaborate oxygenated ring systems. Amide formation and substitution of an available heterocyclic building block are plausible synthetic disconnections for the leading series; the fused aza-core still requires an appropriate precursor. Relative to the Parent, the leading chemistry in seed 1 changes from substituted pyrazole carboxamides to aza-carbazole acetamides, while seed 0 retains the same leading azaindole ester/amide family. This is a change in scaffold arrangement within already abundant ring chemistry.
liabilities: The leading aza-carbazole family has a substantial planar aromatic surface, leaving aqueous behavior and solid-state packing uncertain.
Very long alkyl ester appendages and oversized multifunctional assemblies are still proposed despite their extremely small recorded scores.
Late proposals include hydrazides, a free aryl thiol and adjacent phenols; these add unassessed chemical behavior beyond the leading amide series.
missing_features: The poor proposals often lose the compact combination of aromatic heteroatom placement, an amide linker and limited peripheral bulk seen in the stronger examples; merely retaining aromatic rings does not preserve that arrangement.

The highest digest samples give little coverage of alternative ring topologies carrying a comparable donor/acceptor arrangement, although the Parent supplies a distinct high-scoring pyrazole-amide family.
A specific absent target motif cannot be identified from this score span; the supported gap is reliable coverage of balanced compact arrangements rather than absence of ring or nitrogen chemistry.

Reduced retained learning is a plausible contributor: 481 of 5,220 executed nonterminal steps were discarded, including seven starting-state selections in early sitagliptin optimization. The largest score decline is on that task, but the experiment does not isolate zero-prefix choices or discarded momentum as the cause.

The objective remains misaligned with universal row improvement: 1,217 selected-row exposures have positive, unattainable log-probability targets, and 148 of 420 nonterminal historical groups worsen. These retained properties can limit the usefulness of minimizing the combined fitting loss; neither is a checkpoint execution failure.

Observed core diversity improves on four tasks while utility decreases, so a uniform collapse of sampled core coverage is insufficient to explain the loss. The supplied chemistry assessment still finds concentrated high-score families, undefined stereochemistry and occasional extreme molecular growth; their causal contribution is not isolated.

Selection uses only the already selected accepted current and historical sequences, their original exact strings, and unchanged fixed augmented targets. It changes neither labels nor the membership or replay-memory interfaces.

The zero-dropout recurrent model supports comparable deterministic eval-mode loss measurements without stochastic augmentation. Each selection computation uses the same training-sequence tensor and target; comparisons to other batch-shaped diagnostics allow the explicit numerical tolerance.

Restoring the matching optimizer state is necessary so discarded suffix momentum and step counters cannot affect the next accepted-batch update. Executed work still counts toward the inherited actual optimization receipts.

There is no guaranteed intervention when the final iterate is already the best visited state. An earlier winning prefix can preserve zero net learning for a batch, and repeatedly discarded suffixes can reduce retained learning progress despite unchanged executed work.

Best combined training loss can worsen individual current or historical rows and does not correct positive unattainable targets, preserve unobserved molecular support, or guarantee broader chemistry. Novel generation and endpoint utility require the protocol's actual subsequent evaluations.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two highest-scoring earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current elites, preserving their original accepted strings and scores. The policy fits all selected sequences with equal weight toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward. It takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps and uses the final policy to sample complete SMILES; chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refill the next batch. A passive uniform-history comparator measures the retained score-ordered replay mechanism without contributing to training.
approach.novelty: Add best-prefix checkpoint restoration to online adaptation: after following the existing bounded Adam update path, keep the visited policy and matching optimizer state with the lowest training loss, including the unchanged starting state as an option. This addresses the observed cases where the final iterate has already made the selected examples fit worse. The change selects which completed update prefix survives; it uses the same targets, examples, equal weights and gradient calculations. Earlier siblings changed prior learning, replay membership or retention, and equivalent training strings. None tested whether the last online iterate should be replaced by a better state already visited during the same update. A comparison with the discarded final iterate will establish activation separately from later molecular novelty and score.

The execution claim is also refuted by changed training membership, targets, weights, gradient rule, added optimizer steps or stochastic diagnostic draws. If nonterminal intervention opportunities occur but no earlier checkpoint with a measurable policy difference is retained and no positive terminal-minus-selected loss reduction is observed, the registered activation claim is refuted. Lower target residuals with absent paired score benefit reject the utility prediction without negating checkpoint-selection activation; individual historical worsening alone does not refute this combined-loss mechanism.

Reading all three Parent summary.json and run.log files confirms complete evaluations with macro mean 0.5132724550531974 and population SD 0.001983869060841892; paired changes against n-15499bde2e65 are -0.012215984145254932, +0.00921637067954606 and +0.02015481956958104.
